class TwoPointers:
    # Move Zeroes using Two Pointers
    def move_zeroes_two_pointers(self, nums):
        left = 0  # Pointer for placing non-zero elements

        # Iterate with right pointer
        for right in range(len(nums)):
            if nums[right] != 0:
                # Swap elements if right pointer finds a non-zero
                nums[left], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[left]
                left += 1  # Move left pointer forward

    # Brute Force approach for Container with Most Water
    def max_area_brute_force(self, height):
        n = len(height)
        max_area = 0

        # Check all pairs (i, j)
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                # Compute the minimum height and width
                min_height = min(height[i], height[j])
                width = j - i
                area = min_height * width  # Compute water contained

                max_area = max(max_area, area)  # Update max water
        return max_area

    # Two Pointers approach for Container with Most Water
    def max_area_two_pointers(self, height):
        left, right = 0, len(height) - 1
        max_area = 0

        # Move pointers toward each other
        while left < right:
            width = right - left  # Distance between lines
            min_height = min(height[left], height[right])  # Compute height
            area = min_height * width  # Compute water contained

            max_area = max(max_area, area)  # Update max water

            # Move the pointer pointing to the shorter height
            if height[left] < height[right]:
                left += 1  # Move left pointer forward
            else:
                right -= 1  # Move right pointer backward

        return max_area

Two Pointers Pattern Intuition & Mechanics
text:
The Two Pointers pattern uses two converging or parallel pointers to traverse a linear data structure (typically a sorted array or string) simultaneously. By evaluating conditions across both pointers, it reduces search spaces from O(N^2) brute force to optimal O(N) linear time.

Key Indicators:
- Target array is sorted or can be sorted without violating problem constraints.
- Searching for pairs, triplets, or subsegments satisfying a sum or comparison target.
- Palindrome verification or in-place element swapping (e.g., Two Sum II, 3Sum, Container With Most Water).

Complexity:
- Time Complexity: O(N) or O(N log N) if pre-sorting is required.
- Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Sliding Window Pattern Intuition & Mechanics
text:
The Sliding Window pattern maintains a contiguous subarray or substring boundary defined by two pointers [left, right]. As the right pointer expands the window to include elements, the left pointer shrinks the window when constraints are violated, eliminating redundant recalculations.

Variants:
1. Fixed Window: Window size K remains constant; add incoming element at right, subtract outgoing at left.
2. Dynamic Window: Window expands until a condition is broken, then shrinks left pointer until valid.

Key Indicators:
- Problems involving contiguous subarrays, longest/shortest substrings with K distinct characters, or maximum sum subarray of size K.

Complexity:
- Time Complexity: O(N) as each element is visited at most twice (by left and right pointers).
- Space Complexity: O(K) or O(1) using a hash map or frequency array.

title: Fast & Slow Pointers (Floyd's Cycle Detection)
text:
The Fast and Slow pointer method (Floyd's algorithm) moves two pointers at different speeds (slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps) through a sequence or linked list. If a cycle exists, the fast pointer will eventually lap and meet the slow pointer within the loop.

Applications:
- Linked List Cycle Detection (LeetCode 141, 142).
- Finding the middle of a Linked List in a single pass (slow lands on middle when fast hits null).
- Palindrome Linked List verification.
- Cycle detection in circular arrays and happy number sequences.

Complexity:
- Time Complexity: O(N) traversal.
- Space Complexity: O(1) space.

title: Prefix Sum Pattern Intuition & Mechanics
text:
Prefix Sum precomputes cumulative sums of an array such that prefix[i] = nums[0] + ... + nums[i-1]. This enables O(1) range sum queries between any indices [left, right] via prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left].

When combined with a Hash Map storing running sum frequencies: map[prefix_sum] -> count or earliest index, it solves subarray sum problems (like Subarray Sum Equals K, Continuous Subarray Sum) in single-pass O(N) time.

Complexity:
- Time Complexity: O(N) preprocessing, O(1) per range query.
- Space Complexity: O(N) for prefix array or hash map.

title: Kadane's Algorithm: Maximum Subarray Sum
text:
Kadane's algorithm solves the Maximum Subarray problem in linear time by making a dynamic local choice at each index: either extend the existing running sum with nums[i], or reset and start a new subarray at nums[i].

Intuition:
current_sum = max(nums[i], current_sum + nums[i])
max_sum = max(max_sum, current_sum)
If current_sum drops below 0, carrying it into future indices only penalizes the sum, so we reset.

Complexity:
- Time: O(N), single pass.
- Space: O(1) variables.

title: Monotonic Stack Pattern Intuition & Mechanics
text:
A Monotonic Stack maintains elements in strictly increasing or decreasing order. Whenever an incoming element violates the monotonic invariant, stack elements are popped, revealing the 'Next Greater Element' or 'Next Smaller Element' for every popped item in amortized O(N) time.

Key Indicators:
- Finding the nearest greater/smaller element to the left or right.
- Calculating boundary spans in histogram problems (e.g. Largest Rectangle in Histogram, Trapping Rain Water).
- Online stock span and daily temperatures.

Complexity:
- Time Complexity: O(N) amortized (each element is pushed and popped at most once).
- Space Complexity: O(N) stack capacity.

title: Top K Elements Pattern Using Heaps
text:
To find the K largest or smallest elements in an unsorted collection of size N without sorting the whole array:
- Top K Largest: Maintain a Min-Heap of size K. If current element > min_heap.top(), pop min and push element.
- Top K Smallest: Maintain a Max-Heap of size K.

Key Indicators:
- Finding K-th largest, frequent elements, or K closest points.

Complexity:
- Time Complexity: O(N log K) compared to O(N log N) sorting.
- Space Complexity: O(K) heap storage.

title: Tree Level Order Traversal (Breadth-First Search)
text:
Level Order Traversal explores nodes in a tree or graph level-by-level using a FIFO Queue. At each iteration, we snapshot queue.size() to process all nodes residing on the current depth before advancing.

Key Indicators:
- Shortest path in unweighted graphs or grids.
- Tree zigzag traversal, right/left side views, or minimum depth of binary tree.

Complexity:
- Time: O(V + E) for graphs, O(N) for trees.
- Space: O(W) where W is the maximum width of the tree/graph level.

pattern_name: In-place Reversal of a Linked List
title: In-Place Linked List Reversal Pattern
text:
Reversing a singly linked list in-place utilizes three pointers (prev, curr, next) to flip pointer directions without allocating additional nodes.

Algorithm:
prev = None; curr = head
while curr:
    nxt = curr.next; curr.next = prev; prev = curr; curr = nxt
return prev

Extensions: Reverse sublist between indices [left, right], Reverse Nodes in K-Group.
Complexity: O(N) time, O(1) space.

title: Overlapping Intervals & Merge Technique
text:
Interval problems process intervals [start, end] by sorting them primarily by start time. Once sorted, two intervals [A, B] and [C, D] overlap if and only if C <= B.

Actions:
- Merge: Combined interval is [min(A, C), max(B, D)].
- Conflict / Non-overlapping: Keep interval with earlier end time (Greedy interval scheduling).

Common Problems: Merge Intervals, Non-overlapping Intervals, Meeting Rooms II.
Complexity: O(N log N) due to sorting, O(1) auxiliary space.

pattern_name: Binary Search on Answer / Search Space
title: Binary Search on Continuous & Monotonic Search Spaces
text:
Beyond searching for items in a sorted array, Binary Search applies whenever a decision function check(mid) is monotonic (e.g. FFFTTT or TTTFFF). We set search boundaries [low, high] over the possible answer range and compute mid = low + (high - low) // 2.

Key Indicators:
- Minimax problems ('Minimize the maximum', 'Maximize the minimum allocation').
- Koko Eating Bananas, Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days, Split Array Largest Sum, Aggressive Cows.

Complexity: O(log(range) * cost_of_check).

title: Backtracking Exploration Paradigm
text:
Backtracking incrementally builds candidates for solutions and abandons ('backtracks') as soon as it determines that the candidate cannot lead to a valid full solution.

Template:
def backtrack(path, choices):
    if is_valid_solution(path): results.append(list(path)); return
    for choice in choices:
        if violates_constraints(choice): continue
        make_choice(path, choice)
        backtrack(path, updated_choices)
        undo_choice(path, choice)  # backtrack state

Applications: Subsets, Permutations, Combination Sum, N-Queens, Sudoku Solver.

title: 0/1 Knapsack & Subset Sum Dynamic Programming Pattern
text:
In 0/1 Knapsack, items with weights and values must either be chosen or skipped to maximize value within capacity W. The recurrence: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val[i] + dp[i-1][w - wt[i]]).

Space Optimization:
We can compress the 2D DP table into a 1D array by iterating capacity backwards from W down to wt[i], preventing items from being used multiple times.

Key Problems: Partition Equal Subset Sum, Target Sum, Subset Sum.

title: LCS & String Alignment DP Pattern
text:
LCS finds the longest subsequence present in both strings s1 and s2. If s1[i-1] == s2[j-1], dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else, dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

Variants: Edit Distance, Distinct Subsequences, Shortest Common Supersequence.
Complexity: O(M * N) time and space (compressible to O(min(M, N)) space).

title: Topological Sort for Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG)
text:
Topological ordering arranges DAG vertices linearly such that for every directed edge u -> v, u appears before v.

Kahn's Algorithm (BFS):
1. Calculate in-degree for all vertices.
2. Push vertices with in-degree 0 to queue.
3. While queue is not empty: pop u, append to result, decrement in-degrees of neighbors. If neighbor in-degree reaches 0, push to queue.
4. If result length < V, graph has a cycle!

Applications: Course Schedule I & II, Alien Dictionary, Build Systems.

title: Two Heaps Pattern: Finding Running Median
text:
The Two Heaps pattern balances a Max-Heap for the smaller half of numbers and a Min-Heap for the larger half. The running median is either the top of the max heap (if odd count) or the average of both tops (if even count).

Complexity:
- Insertion: O(log N)
- Find Median: O(1)
Applications: Find Median from Data Stream, Sliding Window Median.

title: Bitwise XOR Properties & Problem Solving
text:
XOR properties:
- a ^ 0 = a
- a ^ a = 0 (self-inverse)
- Commutative and associative: a ^ b ^ a = b

Crucial Tricks:
1. Single Number: XOR all numbers; duplicates cancel out, leaving the unique element.
2. Isolating rightmost set bit: bit = n & (-n)
3. Clearing rightmost set bit: n = n & (n - 1) (Kernighan's bit count).
Complexity: O(1) space, O(N) time.

title: Disjoint Set Union with Path Compression & Union by Rank
text:
Union-Find keeps track of a set of elements partitioned into disjoint subsets.
Optimizations:
- Path Compression in find(x): Flattens the tree so subsequent lookups are O(1).
- Union by Rank/Size: Attaches smaller tree under root of larger tree.

Complexity: Nearly linear O(alpha(N)) amortized time per operation, where alpha is inverse Ackermann.
Applications: Kruskal's MST, Number of Provinces, Redundant Connection.

title: Trie Data Structure & Prefix Matching
text:
A Trie stores strings character by character in a tree structure. Each node has children pointers (usually array of size 26 or hash map) and a boolean flag is_end_of_word.

Operations:
- Insert word: O(L) time where L is word length.
- Search word: O(L) time.
- StartsWith prefix: O(L) time.
Applications: Autocomplete, Spell Check, Maximum XOR Pair (Binary Trie).

title: Segment Tree & Fenwick Tree for Range Queries
text:
Segment Tree and Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick) support logarithmic updates and range queries (sum, min, max, gcd).

Segment Tree:
- Build: O(N)
- Point/Range Update: O(log N) (with Lazy Propagation for range updates)
- Range Query: O(log N)
Applications: Dynamic Range Sum, Range Minimum Query, Count Inversions.
